CausalChain: Gut microbiota-mediated conversion of primary bile acids -> Differential production of secondary bile acids (tumor-promoting DCA, LCA vs tumor-suppressive UDCA) -> Activation of bile acid receptors (FXR, TGR5, VDR) -> Modulation of downstream signaling pathways (apoptosis, inflammation, EMT) -> Cancer cell proliferation and progression are either enhanced or suppressed depending on bile acid profile
Hypothesis: Modulating the gut microbiome to shift bile acid metabolism toward increased production of tumor-suppressive bile acids like UDCA can reprogram nuclear receptor signaling (e.g., FXR and VDR pathways) in cancer cells, thereby inhibiting tumor progression in cancers such as breast, colorectal, and esophageal cancers.
Abstract: Recent studies have highlighted the paradoxical role of bile acids in carcinogenesis, with certain metabolites such as deoxycholic acid and lithocholic acid promoting tumorigenic processes while others, notably ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), exhibit tumor‐suppressive effects. In the gastrointestinal tract, the gut microbiota plays an essential role in the conversion of primary bile acids into secondary bile acids. This conversion, mediated by bile salt hydrolase and dehydroxylation enzymes, influences the spectrum of bile acid species that interact with nuclear and membrane receptors (including FXR, TGR5, and VDR) to regulate cell proliferation, apoptosis, and inflammatory responses. Here we propose that intentional modulation of the gut microbiome to favor the production of tumor-suppressive bile acids such as UDCA can shift receptor signaling toward apoptosis and cell cycle inhibition in cancer cells. Such a change in the bile acid milieu could, at physiological concentrations, reduce epithelial‐mesenchymal transition and impair cancer stem cell properties, especially in gastrointestinal and breast cancers. This hypothesis opens new avenues for therapeutic intervention by repurposing already available drugs and employing targeted probiotic strategies to optimize the bile acid profile.
